Floyd County, Virginia Tax Sales: A Simple Guide to Buying Property at Auction

Floyd County, Virginia holds public tax sales when property owners fall behind on their real estate taxes. These auctions help the county recover lost revenue and give buyers a chance to purchase properties, often at below-market prices. If you’re thinking about joining a tax sale, here’s how it works in clear and easy steps.

Click Here to Get Dustin Hahn’s Tax Lien and Deed FREE Mini-Course

When Floyd County Schedules Tax Sales

Tax sales don’t happen on a fixed schedule. The county announces a sale when there are enough eligible properties.

  • Sale Frequency: As needed
  • Where to Check Dates: Use the Auction Calendar or TACS site for updates

Time and Place of the Auction

Every auction has a set time and location, shared in the official notice.

  • Start Time: Usually begins at 1:00 PM Eastern Time (ET)
  • Where It’s Held:
    • Floyd County Courtroom
    • 100 E. Main Street, Room 200, Floyd, VA 24091

Registration Requirements to Bid

You must register before the auction to place a bid.

  • Is Registration Needed? Yes
  • How to Register:
    • Registration opens when the auction is announced
    • It closes shortly before the event starts
    • All instructions are included in the auction notice

Can Property Owners Redeem Before the Auction?

Yes—but only until the auction date.

  • Before the Auction: Owners can pay all taxes and fees to keep their property
  • After the Auction: They lose the right to redeem

How Bidding and Payment Work

Winning a bid comes with specific payment rules, so be prepared.

  • Who Wins: Highest bidder
  • Deposit Required:
    • $1,000 or 25% of the bid (whichever is higher) due immediately
  • Buyer’s Premium:
    • 10% added to the final bid (minimum $150)
  • Final Payment:
    • Pay remaining balance and deed recording fees within 15 days of court confirmation
  • Accepted Payments:
    • Personal checks
    • Cashier’s checks
    • Traveler’s checks
    • Money orders
    • No cash accepted

Pro Tips for a Smooth Auction Experience

Here are a few smart moves to make before you bid:

  • Look beyond surface-level descriptions—some of the best returns come from overlooked parcels.
  • Attend the auction preview call or inspection if offered—this county sometimes posts updates late.
  • Watch for properties on steep terrain—cheap isn’t always worth it if development costs rise.
